related_questions.question: Is Arizona a zero tolerance DUI state?
related_questions.snippet: Arizona's zero-tolerance policy applies to all drivers and makes it illegal to drive with any amount of alcohol or drugs that impair your ability to operate a vehicle—regardless of age. For drivers under 21, the law is even stricter, prohibiting any measurable amount of alcohol in their system.
related_questions.title: Arizona DUI Laws | DUI Limits | AZ Zero-Tolerance Law

related_questions.question: What happens when you get a DUI for the first-time in Arizona?
related_questions.snippet: The bottom line: Arizona's DUI laws are among the strictest nationwide. A first-time DUI conviction carries mandatory jail time (minimum 10 days, with potential suspensions), fines starting at $1,250, required alcohol screening and education, and installation of an ignition interlock device.
related_questions.title: Arizona DUI Laws: First Offenses, DUI Penalties, and Remedies

related_questions.question: Is your license suspended immediately after a DUI/AZ?
related_questions.snippet: In Arizona, a DUI arrest can result in immediate license suspension or even revocation. For a first offense with a BAC of 0.08% or higher, expect a 90-day suspension, with the possibility of a restricted permit after 30 days.
related_questions.title: Do You Get Your License Suspended After a DUI in Arizona?

related_questions.question: How to avoid jail time for DUI in AZ?
related_questions.snippet: Arizona law for a first-time standard DUI imposes a minimum 10-day jail term. It is possible, however, for a judge to reduce this to as little as one day, with the other nine days being suspended, if you complete alcohol or drug abuse treatment, counseling, and screening.

text_blocks.snippet: In Arizona, a DUI (Driving Under the Influence) charge can be triggered by impairment from alcohol or drugs, with a BAC of .08% or higher for those 21 and older. For those under 21, any measurable amount of alcohol in their system can lead to a DUI. Refusal to take a chemical test can result in a one-year license suspension for a first offense, and two years for subsequent offenses.
snippet_highlighted_words: a DUI (Driving Under the Influence) charge can be triggered by impairment from alcohol or drugs, with a BAC of .08% or higher for those 21 and older

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Arizona DUI laws include:

list.title: BAC Levels:
list.snippet: .08% or higher for those 21+, .04% for commercial drivers, and any measurable amount for those under 21.

list.title: Implied Consent:
list.snippet: By driving in Arizona, drivers agree to submit to chemical tests for alcohol or drugs if requested by law enforcement.

list.title: Aggravated DUI:
list.snippet: A DUI becomes a felony if the driver's license is suspended, it's the third DUI in seven years, a minor is in the car, or the driver is on the wrong side of the highway.

list.title: Penalties:
list.snippet: Penalties for DUI can include jail time, fines, license suspension, ignition interlock device installation, and mandatory alcohol screening/counseling.

list.title: First Offense:
list.snippet: A first-time DUI can result in a minimum of 10 days in jail, though it may be reduced to one day with alcohol/drug treatment.

list.title: Extreme and Super Extreme DUIs:
list.snippet: A BAC of .15% to .19% elevates the charge to an Extreme DUI, while .20% or more is considered a Super Extreme DUI, resulting in harsher penalties.

list.title: Second and Third Offenses:
list.snippet: A second DUI within seven years results in more severe penalties, and a third DUI within seven years is a felony.
Arizona has a zero-tolerance policy for drivers under 21, meaning any BAC above 0.00% can lead to a DUI charge.
Underage drivers can also face aggravated DUI charges if aggravating factors are present.
A DUI becomes a felony in Arizona if it involves a suspended license, is the third DUI within seven years, if a minor is in the vehicle, or if other aggravating factors are present.
